title: HomeFlood Renewal Surcharge for Nonpayment Notices
content:
**Rule.** A HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies renewal term premium carries a payment-history surcharge. The surcharge counts the notices of cancellation for nonpayment (NONPAYMENT) mailed on the policy in the 12 whole months before the booking date.

| Nonpayment notices mailed in that window | Surcharge |
|---|---|
| two or more | 6 percent |
| exactly one | 3 percent |
| none | none |

**Form of the surcharge.** The surcharge is a percent of the premium the renewal term premium starts from, and it is added to that premium.

**The booking date.** The booking date is the day the renewal is booked and recorded, and every window and length of time counted to the booking date ends on that day.

**The window.** A notice falls within the window when the whole calendar months from its mailing date to the booking date are fewer than 12. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

**Which notices count.** Only notices with the reason nonpayment count. A notice of cancellation for material misrepresentation, and a non-renewal notice, are not counted.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a renewal booked on 15 August, with nonpayment notices mailed on 20 August of the previous year and on 3 February of the booking year, counts both notices. The first is 11 whole months back, because the 15th falls before the 20th. The surcharge is therefore 6 percent.
